who: Florence C. Hsia, historian of science at Wisconsin–Madison; PhD in history, Chicago, 1999.

evidence.says: Wisconsin faculty profile identifies Florence C. Hsia as a historian of science and lists a Chicago history PhD in 1999.
The 2018 PhD recipients list names Florence Hsia among Nicholas A. Jacobson's advisors.
LC identifies Florence C. Hsia, author of Sojourners in a Strange Land (2009), as associate professor of history of science at Wisconsin–Madison.

notes: The LC candidate's affiliation, field and work identify the Wisconsin supervisor; the doctorate matches exactly.

who: Sung Bok Kim, historian of early America at SUNY Albany from 1973; PhD, Michigan State, 1966.

evidence.says: AHA records his Michigan State PhD in 1966, appointment at Albany in 1973, and authorship of Landlord and Tenant in Colonial New York (1978).
Albany's 2001 faculty announcement identifies Sung Bok Kim as a colonial American historian and author of Landlord and Tenant in Colonial New York.
LC's Sung Bok Kim authority cites Landlord and Tenant in Colonial New York (1978).
The alternative candidate Sungeun Kim's ORCID lists an assistant professorship in Korea University's Division of International Studies beginning in 2025.

notes: The LC candidate is the Albany historian: book, institution, field and doctorate agree. The alternative ORCID provides no corroboration for this match.

who: Leonard Krieger, historian of modern European intellectual history, formerly at Yale and later Chicago; Yale PhD, 1949.

evidence.says: The Institute for Advanced Study records Leonard Krieger's Yale PhD in 1949.
Yale lists Krieger's Liberal Ideas and Institutions in the German Era of Unification among its 1949 dissertations.
The encyclopedia identifies Krieger as a Yale history professor in 1961 who moved to Chicago in 1962, and as author of The German Idea of Freedom.
LC identifies the historian Leonard Krieger through The German Idea of Freedom (1957) and records his later Chicago history professorship.

notes: The candidate's work and Yale doctorate establish the identity. His move to Chicago in 1962 preceded the listed students' completion years, so those years should not be treated as dates of Yale employment.

who: Warren F. Kuehl, historian of internationalism and foreign relations at Mississippi State, 1958–1964; Northwestern PhD, 1954.

evidence.says: Richard W. Leopold's memorial in the March 1988 SHAFR newsletter, pp. 1–2, records Kuehl's Northwestern doctorate in 1954, dissertation The Life and Work of Hamilton Holt, 1872–1925, and Mississippi State service from 1958 to 1964.
LC's Warren F. Kuehl authority cites The Life and Work of Hamilton Holt, 1872–1925 (1954).

notes: The candidate's dissertation identifies the same historian; his Mississippi State appointment covers all three listed students' years.

who: Semion Lyandres, historian of modern Russia at Notre Dame; Stanford PhD, 1992.

evidence.says: Notre Dame identifies Lyandres as professor emeritus of history, a faculty fellow since 2001, with a Stanford PhD in 1992; publications include The Bolsheviks' German Gold Revisited and A Chronicle of the Civil War in Siberia and Exile in China.
LC identifies Semion Lyandres through those same two works, with an author-supplied full name of Semion Mikhailovich Lyandres.
Notre Dame's 2004–2005 bulletin lists Semion Lyandres in history, appointed in 2000, with a Stanford PhD in 1992.

notes: The candidate's works identify the Notre Dame historian, whose doctorate and appointment fit the supervisor record.

who: Patrick E. Martin, industrial archaeologist at Michigan Tech; PhD in anthropology, Michigan State, 1984.

evidence.says: Michigan Tech's repository names Patrick E. Martin as Sean Gohman's dissertation advisor for the 2018 PhD on Michigan copper mining.
Michigan Tech identifies Patrick E. Martin as professor emeritus of archaeology, specializing in industrial archaeology, with a Michigan State anthropology PhD in 1984.
The candidate Patricia Preciado Martin is an author of oral-history collections and short stories, including Songs My Mother Sang to Me and El Milagro and Other Stories.
LC identifies Patricia Preciado Martin through Songs My Mother Sang to Me and La Frontera Perspective.

notes: The sole candidate is a different author. The supplied LSU history doctorate in 1974 also conflicts with the directly identified Michigan Tech supervisor's degree.

who: Wolfgang P. Mueller, medieval legal historian at Fordham; Syracuse PhD in medieval/early modern history, 1991.

evidence.says: Fordham identifies Wolfgang P. Mueller as a medieval church-law historian with a Syracuse PhD in 1991.
His CV lists Fordham history appointments from 2000, covering the students' 2012–2018 completion years.
The Austrian Academy identifies the candidate's ORCID 0000-0002-6674-0605 with Wolfgang Mueller, professor of Russian history at Vienna, whose works concern Soviet policy, Austria and the Cold War.
Stanford's profile of this contemporary historian records a PhD in contemporary history and Russian studies from Vienna.

notes: The candidate is the Vienna contemporary historian; the supervisor is Fordham's medievalist. Their institutions, fields and doctoral universities differ.

who: Tiffany Ruby Patterson, historian of the African diaspora at Binghamton, 1994–2005; Minnesota PhD, 1995.

evidence.says: Patterson's CV records a Minnesota history PhD and Binghamton appointments in history and Africana studies: assistant professor, 1994–2002, and associate professor, 2002–2005.
Vanderbilt lists Tiffany Ruby Patterson's Minnesota PhD in 1995 and her book Zora Neale Hurston and a History of Southern Life (2005).
LC identifies Tiffany Ruby Patterson through that book and describes her as an associate professor of history at Binghamton.

notes: Full name, book, doctoral university and year agree. The CV places her at Binghamton for the 2002 and 2003 students; the 2006 completion follows her move in 2005.
